To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
contiguous Hyps are the major sites of O arabinoside addition in plant cell wall HRGPs.
contiguous hydroxyproline (Hyp) residues are the major sites of Hyp O arabinoside formation in the hydroxyprolyne rich glycoprotein of Douglas fir (Pronase digest).
the extent of HRGPs arabinosylation is positively correlated with the contiguity (i.e. number) of their hydroxyproline sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of a HRGP and the elucidation of the glycosylation code for this class of glycoproteins.
the elucidation of the glycosylation code of HRGPs and with the determination of their structures and molecular masses.
the elucidation of the structure of the arabinosyl residues in the HRGP from Douglas fir, and the determination of their site of attachment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
contiguous Hyp are the major sites of O arabinosylations in HRGPs.
Hyp contiguity is a prerequisite for Hyp O arabinosilation, but is not sufficient for Hyp O arabi-nosylation.
the Hyp contiguities hypothesis is correct for the PHRGPs of P. menziesii.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tandem mass spectrometric analysis of glycopeptides from HRGPs provides a rapid and sensitive means of elucidating the glycosylation sites of HRGPs and is consistent with the hypothesis that contiguous Hyp residues are the major sites of HRGP arabinosylation.
contiguous Hyp residues are the major site of Hyp arabinosylaton in plant cell wall glycoproteins.
the arabinosides in the PHRGP from Douglas fir are O linked to Hyp residues, and that the arabinose chains are predominantly triarabinofuranosides attached to contiguous Hyp residues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

tandem mass spectrometric analysis of HRGPs is a powerful method for elucidating their glycosylation sites and structures, and for the first time we can now test our Hyp contiguity arabinosylation hypothesis.
tandem mass spectrometric methods are powerful tools to determine arabinosylation sites in HRGPs, and we anticipate that this approach will facilitate the elucidation of the HRGP glycosylation code.
tandem mass spectrometric analysis of HRGP glycopeptides is a powerful approach for determining arabinosylation sites in HRGPs.
